title: Tight Global Bound on Pairwise Entanglement of Formation in Three-Qubit Systems
authors: Wei Song, Xiao-Lan Zong, Ming Yang
abstract: We derive a global bound on the sum of pairwise squared entanglement of formation in three-qubit systems. The bound is tight and can be saturated by states containing a maximally entangled bipartite pair with an uncorrelated third qubit. Moreover, using this relation, we can map the three bipartite entanglements to three coordinates, such that any three-qubit state corresponds to a point in three-dimensional space, thereby endowing this global inequality with a very natural geometric picture. Accordingly, the dynamical evolution can be interpreted as trajectories in this geometric space; we select representative initial states and investigate the dynamical behavior of the three pairwise entanglements under various Markovian noise models.
summary: This paper establishes a tight global upper bound on the sum of pairwise squared entanglement of formation for three-qubit systems. It provides a natural geometric picture by mapping the three bipartite entanglements to coordinates constrained by this inequality. Furthermore, it analyzes how this entanglement structure decays over time under various quantum noise models.
main_problem: The paper aims to derive a global upper bound on the sum of pairwise squared entanglement of formation ($	ext{EOF}^2$) in three-qubit systems, extending beyond traditional monogamy relations.
main_result: A global inequality $	ext{EOF}^2(ho_{AB}) + 	ext{EOF}^2(ho_{AC}) + 	ext{EOF}^2(ho_{BC}) \leq 1$ was derived for any three-qubit state, which is shown to be tight.
method: The authors used mathematical techniques involving the binary entropy function and optimization over a polytope defined by entanglement measures to establish the global bound.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Geometric representation of the global pairwise EOF constraint. Blue points denote 105 Haar-random three-qubit pure states plotted in the coordinates (RAB, RAC, RBC) = (E2 f(ρAB), E2 f(ρAC), E2 f(ρBC)). The states remain below the saturation plane RAB + RAC + RBC = 1. The vertices cor- respond to Bell-pair conﬁgurations. The GHZ and W states indicate the opposite limits of absent and distributed pairwise entanglement.

FIG. 2. Haar-random sampling of three-qubit pure states in the (MEOF, τ3) plane. The quantity MEOF = E2 f(ρAB) + E2 f(ρAC) + E2 f(ρBC) is the total pairwise squared entangle- ment of formation, while τ3 is the three-tangle. The GHZ, W , and Bell-pair states identify three distinct correlation struc- tures: genuine tripartite entanglement, distributed pairwise entanglement, and concentrated pairwise entanglement.

FIG. 3. Normalized pairwise squared-EOF survival function under global depolarizing noise. The W and D(2) 3 states show the same decay curve due to their local-unitary equivalence and the covariance of the depolarizing channel. In contrast, the Bell-pair state follows a diﬀerent decay behavior, reﬂect- ing the fact that its pairwise EOF is localized in one two-qubit subsystem.

FIG. 4. Normalized pairwise squared-EOF survival function under local amplitude damping. Although the W and D(2) 3 states have the same initial pairwise EOF, they exhibit dif- ferent decay behaviors due to their diﬀerent excitation struc- tures.

Figure 3 presents the dynamical evolution under global depolarizing noise. Since the W and D(2) 3 state can be transformed into each other by local bit-ﬂip opera- tions, and the depolarizing channel preserves local uni- tary equivalence, they have identical decay curves. In contrast, under the normalized representation, the Bell- pair state decays more slowly, which is consistent with its feature that the pairwise EOF is concentrated in a single two-qubit subsystem. In contrast to depolarizing noise, amplitude damping is sensitive to the number of excitations in the quantum state.
